text:
We checked “Fact-Sheet-Images_Bad” and found 3 issues in the InDesign file that are likely causing the problems in Frontify, plus 3 that may change how it looks. Here’s what to change:

Likely causing the problems

1. Text frame has no paragraph style
Frontify uses paragraph styles to format text and decide what can be edited.
Where: text frames “FACT SHEET”, “Summer Collection 2020”, “Icatur aut ut aut qui sequi cum…” (page 1) and 1 more
• Select the frame and apply a paragraph style in Window > Styles > Paragraph Styles (any style except [Basic Paragraph] or [No Paragraph Style]).
Learn more

2. Text without a paragraph style
Frontify uses paragraph styles to format text and decide what can be edited.
Where: 3 text frames on page 1
Tip: some of this is only spaces or empty lines after the text. Delete them, or give them a style too.
• Select the text and apply a paragraph style in Window > Styles > Paragraph Styles (any style except [Basic Paragraph] or [No Paragraph Style]).
Learn more

3. Font missing from the package
Frontify needs the font files to render the text, otherwise the template falls back to another font.
Where: the font “Minion Pro”
• Make sure the font is installed or activated on your computer.
• Package again with File > Package with "Copy Fonts" checked, and zip the whole folder, including "Document fonts".
Learn more

May change how it looks

4. Hyphenation is on
Browsers hyphenate differently from InDesign, so lines may break in different places.
Where: paragraph styles “Title” and “Text”, used on page 1
• In the paragraph style, go to Hyphenation and uncheck Hyphenate.
Learn more

5. Text formatted outside its paragraph style
Formatting added by hand on top of a paragraph style (shown as a + next to the style name) may be lost or look different in Frontify.
Where: text frames “FACT SHEET” (page 1, font and tracking changed), “Summer Collection 2020” (page 1, font, size and leading changed), “Icatur aut ut aut qui sequi cum…” (page 1, font, size and leading changed) and 5 more
• Click into the text. A + after the style name in Window > Styles > Paragraph Styles means it has extra formatting.
• To remove it, select the text and click Clear Overrides at the bottom of the Paragraph Styles panel.
• To keep the look, update the style to match instead (right-click the style > Redefine Style), or use a character style for single words.
Learn more

6. Paragraph Composer used
The Adobe Paragraph Composer breaks lines differently from browsers, so text may reflow in Frontify.
Where: paragraph styles “[Basic Paragraph]”, “Text” and “Title”, used on page 1
• In the paragraph style, go to Justification and set Composer to Adobe Single-line Composer.
Learn more

Once that’s done, package the document again with File > Package, zip the package folder and upload it to Frontify.
